concepts.name: Control of fire
concepts.summary: Keeping, feeding and using fire deliberately for warmth, light, protection and cooking.

concepts.name: Fire-making
concepts.summary: Kindling fire on demand by percussion or friction instead of keeping or collecting it.

concepts.name: Managed landscape burning
concepts.summary: Setting regular, planned fires to shape vegetation, game and travel across a whole country.

concepts.name: Coal as fuel
concepts.summary: Mining and burning coal as a routine fuel for heating and industry in place of wood.

concepts.name: Petroleum fuels
concepts.summary: Producing crude oil in quantity and refining it into lamp oil and engine fuels.

concepts.name: Draught animal traction
concepts.summary: Yoking or harnessing animals to pull ploughs, sledges and vehicles.

concepts.name: Pack animal transport
concepts.summary: Carrying loads over distance on the backs of domesticated animals led in trains.

concepts.name: Camel caravan transport
concepts.summary: Using camels as pack and riding animals to carry trade across deserts.

concepts.name: Windmill
concepts.summary: A fixed machine that turns wind into rotary power for grinding or pumping.

concepts.name: Internal combustion engine
concepts.summary: An engine that burns its fuel inside the working cylinder.

concepts.name: Compression-ignition engine
concepts.summary: An engine that ignites heavy fuel by the heat of compression alone, at high efficiency.

concepts.name: Incandescent electric lighting
concepts.summary: A durable filament lamp, with the supply system that makes electric light usable in ordinary rooms.

concepts.name: Transformer-based alternating-current distribution
concepts.summary: Sending electricity at high voltage and stepping it down with transformers for use.

concepts.name: Rechargeable battery
concepts.summary: A cell that stores electrical energy chemically and can be charged again many times.

concepts.name: Nuclear power station
concepts.summary: A reactor that supplies electricity to a public grid.

concepts.name: Photovoltaic cell
concepts.summary: A solid-state cell that turns sunlight directly into useful electric power.

concepts.name: Wind-powered electricity generation
concepts.summary: Generating electricity from a wind-driven turbine.

concepts.name: Air conditioning
concepts.summary: Controlling the temperature and humidity of indoor air by machine.

concepts.name: Wheeled vehicle
concepts.summary: A load-carrying vehicle that rolls on wheels turning on or with an axle.

concepts.name: Horseback riding
concepts.summary: Riding horses for travel, herding and war.

concepts.name: Bicycle
concepts.summary: A human-powered two-wheeled vehicle fit for everyday travel.

concepts.name: Automobile
concepts.summary: A self-propelled road vehicle driven by an engine it carries.

concepts.name: Railway track
concepts.summary: Guiding wheeled wagons along fixed rails so that a given effort moves a far greater load.

concepts.name: Public steam railway
concepts.summary: A railway worked by locomotives carrying paying passengers and goods to a timetable.

concepts.name: Electric rail traction
concepts.summary: Driving trains and trams by electric motors supplied from fixed conductors.

concepts.name: Open-sea voyaging
concepts.summary: Crossing stretches of open sea in watercraft with enough people to settle the far shore.

concepts.name: Dugout canoe
concepts.summary: A boat hollowed from a single log.

concepts.name: Plank-built boat
concepts.summary: A hull assembled from shaped planks fastened edge to edge, free of the size of any one tree.

concepts.name: Sail
concepts.summary: Using the wind to drive a boat.

concepts.name: Outrigger canoe
concepts.summary: A narrow hull steadied by a float held out on booms, able to carry sail at sea.

concepts.name: Clinker shipbuilding
concepts.summary: Building light, flexible hulls from overlapping planks riveted together.

concepts.name: Stern-mounted rudder
concepts.summary: Steering a vessel with a rudder hung on its centreline at the stern.

concepts.name: Frame-first shipbuilding
concepts.summary: Setting up a skeleton of keel and frames and then fastening the planking to it.

concepts.name: Full-rigged ocean ship
concepts.summary: A multi-masted ship combining square and fore-and-aft sails, able to stay at sea for months.

concepts.name: Steam navigation
concepts.summary: Driving vessels by engine, independent of wind and current.

concepts.name: Monsoon sailing
concepts.summary: Timing open-ocean passages to the seasonal reversal of the monsoon winds.

concepts.name: Celestial latitude navigation
concepts.summary: Finding position north or south at sea by measuring the height of the Sun or stars.

concepts.name: Satellite navigation
concepts.summary: Fixing position anywhere on Earth from the signals of orbiting satellites.

concepts.name: Balloon flight
concepts.summary: Lifting people off the ground with a bag of hot air or light gas.

concepts.name: Powered controlled flight
concepts.summary: Sustained flight of a heavier-than-air machine under its own power and the pilot's control.

concepts.name: Turbojet engine
concepts.summary: A gas turbine that drives an aircraft by the thrust of its exhaust.

concepts.name: Liquid-propellant rocket
concepts.summary: A rocket burning liquid fuel and oxidiser, controllable and powerful enough to reach space.

concepts.name: Artificial satellite
concepts.summary: Placing a made object in orbit around the Earth.

concepts.name: Human spaceflight
concepts.summary: Carrying people into space and bringing them back alive.

concepts.name: Intermodal container shipping
concepts.summary: Moving goods in standard boxes that pass between ship, rail and lorry without being unpacked.

concepts.name: Refrigerated shipping
concepts.summary: Carrying perishable food across oceans under mechanical refrigeration.

origins.title: Controlled use of fire by early humans in southern Africa
origins.where: Wonderwerk Cave, Northern Cape, South Africa
origins.why: Fire gave cooking, warmth, light and protection, and every later heat technology from pottery to smelting stands on it.
origins.verify: Pin down the earliest secure in-situ evidence of burning inside a habitation (Wonderwerk c. 1.0 Ma) against the older, disputed open-air claims (Koobi Fora, Chesowanja, Swartkrans), and when use became habitual rather than occasional (Gesher Benot Ya'aqov c. 780 ka, Qesem Cave c. 400-300 ka). Say which hominin is implicated.
